item: An article whose page was fetched from another site says so beside the source it is credited to (queue item 61)
summary: Queue item 61, the follow-up R635 named (feeds stay unscoped; a feed item's link is followed wherever it redirects, after that host's robots.txt). BEFORE: an article a feed item's redirect fetched from another site was credited to the source with nothing saying where the page came from: Article.url is the address ASKED for, and the final address was dropped. NOW: Article.fetched_host (VARCHAR 255, nullable, Alembic f61a2b3c4d5e on c4e8a2d6f1b9, plus the boot self-heal ensure_article_fetched_host_column registered in SELF_HEALED_COLUMNS, init_db and the scale bench) holds the host of the address the fetch ENDED on: src.utils.url_utils.fetched_host, urllib.parse's .hostname (lower-cased, no login, no port, IPv6 without brackets, cut at 255), None when unreadable. Written by src.ingest.pipeline (which ingest_url and store_fetched use: feeds, crawl, sitemap, archive backfill, markets, manual URL ingest) and by the collector's per-source batch. NULL is 'not recorded', never a guess: articles stored before the column, imported newsletters, and the paths that store without that fetch (Wikipedia, law, hazards, IPCC, statistics). Whether it is ANOTHER SITE is computed at read time against Source.domain by off_the_source_site, which is src.ingest.host_mismatch.check_host (registrable domain through the bundled Public Suffix List, the quarantine host-mismatch report's own comparison): a source's own subdomain is its site (en.yna.co.kr for yna.co.kr), a public suffix is never a site, Unicode and punycode agree, two sites url_utils.DOMAIN_ALIASES names as one are one site (bbc.co.uk for bbc.com, as the quarantine's own check reads them), a trailing dot is left out of the comparison, and UNKNOWN (an IP, a top-level domain the list has no rule for, an unreadable domain) says nothing (null), never 'another site'. Shown: the reader (/api/articles/{id}/view) beside the source's name (' · Fetched from another site <host>') and as a 'Fetched from (app-observed, after redirects)' row with ' · Not the source's site (<domain>)', the three phrases their own text nodes keyed in all 12 locales (the page's i18n walker translates them) and the host and domain in their own <code>, escaped; the /api/articles rows, the Home feed's cards (/api/feed) and Home's Latest panel (/api/insights/latest) as fetched_host and fetched_off_site, through one helper (url_utils.fetched_host_fields) shared with the briefing-card audit report (card_audit, a diagnostics report, not the card's own evidence rows); the SPA rows that render them (Explore's list and table, the corpus table, the synthesis picker, Home's most-recent rows, the Feed cards and the Latest panel) through ooFetchedOffSiteNote in app-core.js, ' · fetched from <host>' with the hover 'This article is credited to the source, but the stored page was fetched from another site.' (both keyed in all 12 locales); the investigate page's coverage table, through its own copy of the note (that page does not load the engine), with the same two strings; the CSV export as a trailing 'Fetched From Host' column (every earlier column in place) and the JSON export and the collect pass's opt-in delta export (runlog.export_delta, when export_dir is set) as fetched_host; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and USER_MANUAL.md say so, and that a field added beside the others does not bump oo-export-N. A backup merge carries it on a NEW article and never adopts it onto a hash duplicate (in _NOT_ADOPTABLE_ARTICLE_COLUMNS with the url argument: a hash twin is often another source's copy of the same wire story, fetched from its own site). The downgrade drops the column in place (op.drop_column), never through batch_alter_table, which rebuilds the table without its triggers. TESTS: tests/test_fetched_host_item61.py (69), through the real EthicalFetcher over an in-memory session, the real ingest_url and the real batch, the real routes over a file-backed store (TestClient), the real merge_corpus and the real Alembic downgrade/upgrade; tests/fetched_host_node_test.js runs both copies of the note, the SPA's extracted from the shipped engine and the investigate page's from its script; on 7b19072ce, with the new names imported behind a guard, all 69 fail or error (62 and 7: the column does not exist there), and the node test fails (the helper is not there). Two existing tests the first build broke are fixed: test_source_composite_key's staged-copy migration test expects the new head, and rewalk_b22_node_test.js's sandboxes load the helper. MUTANTS: 35 on the first folded head, 34 killed; the one survivor is equivalent (dropping off_the_source_site's empty-input guard, a fast path check_host answers the same way). 16 more on the second fold (the alias, either trailing dot, the Latest panel's fields, its domain and its column, the delta export, the reader's words as their own nodes and the host in its <code>, the SPA's Latest row, and the investigate page's escaping, strict check, hover and fallback, a locale key): 15 killed, and the survivor (the dot kept on the source's domain) killed by two cases added for it. INDEPENDENT READ (Opus) of the first build: NO-GO, three must-fixes, folded: (1) the two broken tests; (2) 'another site' used the crawl's same-site rule, so some 50 enabled catalogue sources that publish on a subdomain of their listed domain would have read as fetched from another site on every article (their probe: en.yna.co.kr, english.kyodonews.net, ici.radio-canada.ca, edition.cnn.com, about.gitlab.com); (3) the merge adopted the host onto a hash duplicate (their probe: source A's wire story took source B's host). Should-fixes folded: the batch downgrade lost the articles triggers (their probe), the Feed and the investigate page were not covered, the export docs said the CSV columns were unchanged, the hover claimed the feed's link led there (false for a manual URL ingest), the model comment's NULL list. A FRESH INDEPENDENT READ (Opus) of the folded head: GO, with should-fixes, folded: the investigate page's copy of the note was untested (two of their mutants survived there); bbc.com and bbc.co.uk read as two sites, where the quarantine's own check reads them as one; Home's Latest panel and the delta export credited the source without the host; the reader's words were English inside a translated page; nits. NOT CHANGED, stated: these rows credit the source from endpoints that do not carry the host, and each links to the reader, which shows it: a briefing card's own evidence rows on Home (the audit report carries it, the card does not), keyword-in-context, the claim table and the claim trail, near-duplicate clusters, articles-by-link, the synthesis citations, and the per-source server-IP view; an operator-confirmed host-mismatch pair (R193/R195) is not consulted, so such a source's articles still say where they were fetched from, a fact rather than a flag; no backfill (the redirects of stored articles were never kept); a backup merge still adopts server_ip onto a hash duplicate, as it did before; if the bundled Public Suffix List cannot be read, every answer is unknown and the notes say nothing; an IP-literal host says nothing. Release-notes line: «An article whose link led to another site now says so: the reader, the article lists, the Home feed and its latest articles, and the exports show the site the page was actually fetched from beside the source it is credited to.»
